# Importing R packages


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, sfdep, sf, tmap, spdep)
```
:::


# Importing data into R


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
hunan <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial", 
                 layer = "Hunan") %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 32650)
```

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
hunan2012 <- read_csv("data/aspatial/Hunan_2012.csv")
```
:::


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
hunan_GDPPC <- left_join(hunan, hunan2012) %>%
  select(1:4, 7, 15)
```
:::


::: panel-tabset
# sfdep
Compute weights matrix with sfdep

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
wm_q <- hunan_GDPPC %>%
  mutate(nb=st_contiguity(geometry),
         wt=st_weights(nb, 
                       style="W"),
         .before=1 #place any new columns created at the very beginning of the data frame.
  )
```
:::


# spdep

Compute continuity matrix with spdep 

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
wm_q_spdep <- poly2nb(hunan, queen=TRUE)
```
:::

compute row standardised weight matrix with spdep

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
rswm_q <- nb2listw(wm_q_spdep, 
                   style="W", 
                   zero.policy = TRUE)
rswm_q
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}


sfdep is an improvement on spdep because it can compute the weights matrix without intermediate steps, and it is easier to see the results in relation to the original table/locations without additional steps

# Global Moran's I

:::panel-tabset
# sfdep
Calculate Global Moran's I

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(1234) #ensure reproducibility of results
global_moran_perm(
  wm_q$GDPPC, 
  wm_q$nb, 
  wm_q$wt, 
  nsim=99 #100 simulations
  )
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Monte-Carlo simulation of Moran I

data:  x 
weights: listw  
number of simulations + 1: 100 

statistic = 0.30075, observed rank = 100, p-value < 2.2e-16
alternative hypothesis: two.sided
```


:::
:::

As p value <0.05, we reject the null hypothesis that the spatial distribution of GDP per capita resembles a random distirbution (ie are spatially independent). As the Moran's I statistic is greater than 0, we can infer that the GDP per capita is spatially clustered at the county level.

#spdep

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
bperm= moran.mc(hunan_GDPPC$GDPPC, 
                listw=rswm_q, 
                nsim=999, 
                zero.policy = TRUE, 
                na.action=na.omit)
bperm
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Monte-Carlo simulation of Moran I

data:  hunan_GDPPC$GDPPC 
weights: rswm_q  
number of simulations + 1: 1000 

statistic = 0.30075, observed rank = 1000, p-value = 0.001
alternative hypothesis: greater
```


:::
:::

:::
sfdep allows the test to be performed using different columns within a single table

# Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(1234)
lisa <- wm_q %>%
  mutate(local_moran=local_moran(
    GDPPC, nb, wt, nsim=99),
    .before=1) %>%
  unnest(local_moran) 
```
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
glimpse(lisa)
```

:::

plot LISA 

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
lisa <- lisa %>%
  mutate(
    LISA_cluster = ifelse(
      p_ii_sim < 0.05,
      as.character(mean), 
      "Insignificant"), 
    LISA_cluster = factor(
      LISA_cluster,
      levels = c("Insignificant", "Low-Low", "Low-High", "High-Low", "High-High")
    )
  )
```
:::


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
lisa_map <- tm_shape(lisa) + 
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "LISA_cluster",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(
      values = c(
        "grey80",      # Insignificant
        "blue",        # Low-Low
        "lightblue",   # Low-High
        "pink",        # High-Low
        "red"          # High-High
      )
    ),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(
      title = "LISA Cluster",
      position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"))
  ) +
  tm_borders() +
  tm_title("Local Moran's I Clusters (p < 0.05)")
lisa_map
```
